Equipment is tracked through the Inventory Grid.

This is not a weight system.
It is a space and load system that shows how much gear a character can carry while still moving and reacting cleanly.

Each item occupies a number of squares in the grid based on its listed size.

Inventory Grid

Each character has an Inventory Grid of 24 × 9 squares.

The grid is divided into three load zones, each 8 columns wide:

  • Zone 1: Normal Load
  • Zone 2: Encumbered
  • Zone 3: Overloaded

The further right an item is placed, the more difficult the total load becomes to carry efficiently.

If all carried items fit completely inside Zone 1, the character is under Normal Load.

If any part of an item reaches into Zone 2, the character becomes Encumbered.

If any part of an item reaches into Zone 3, the character becomes Overloaded.

Only the highest occupied zone matters.

Load Effects

  • Normal Load: no penalty
  • Encumbered: Movement −4 m
  • Overloaded: Movement -6 m

Load does not prevent carrying gear.
It represents how difficult that gear is to carry efficiently in an active situation.

Item Placement

Each item has an Inventory Size written as width × height.

To place an item into the Inventory Grid:

  • the item must fit entirely within empty squares
  • items may not overlap
  • items must be placed as one continuous rectangle
  • an item’s position determines whether it remains in Normal Load or pushes the character into a higher load zone

If even a single square of an item extends into a higher zone, that item counts as occupying that zone.

Item sizes are listed in the item entry, equipment list, or VTT data.

Item Rotation

Items may be rotated by 90 degrees when placed in the Inventory Grid.

This changes the item from width × height to height × width.

Rotation is allowed only if the rotated item still fits entirely into empty squares.

If at least one item reaches into Zone 3, the character is Overloaded.

Example Layout

In this example, the character’s load state depends on the furthest zone occupied by any item.

If all items remain inside Zone 1, the character is under Normal Load.
If at least one item reaches into Zone 2, the character is Encumbered.
If at least one item reaches into Zone 3, the character is Overloaded.

Dropping Load

A character may drop carried gear to remove Encumbered or Overloaded.

If a character is surprised while Encumbered or Overloaded, they must decide whether to fight while carrying the load or spend Attack Actions to drop it safely.

If the gear is dropped hastily, it can be done immediately with GM approval, but the character accepts the risk that items inside are damaged, scattered, lost, or exposed.

The GM should only apply this consequence when it matters.

Examples:

  • glass bottles shatter
  • oil leaks
  • arrows spill
  • rations are ruined
  • tools scatter
  • a lantern breaks
  • a scroll case pops open
  • fragile loot is damaged

Surprise and Load

If a character is surprised while Encumbered or Overloaded, they must decide whether to fight while carrying the load or spend Attack Actions to drop it safely.

This makes heavy preparation a tactical risk without adding extra math.

Summary

Load State Trigger Movement Safely Drop Load
Normal Only Zone 1 occupied Normal Free / no issue
Encumbered Any item in Zone 2 −4 m 1 Attack Action
Overloaded Any item in Zone 3 −6 m 2 Attack Actions

Weapon Properties

Property Description
Finesse Attack Roll uses Agility (for To-Hit only, not for damage).
Light May be wielded in the off-hand.
Versatile When wielded two-handed, gain +2d8 weapon damage (you lose your shield / off-hand).
Reach (+1 m / +2 m) Your melee reach is 2 m by default; this increases it. Measure from the attacker’s token center for a single-Hex creature, or from the nearest edge of its occupied footprint for a multi-Hex creature using Growth.
Heavy You get –10 to your Initiative roll.
Balanced If a weapon has Heavy + Balanced, reduce the Heavy penalty to –5 Initiative.
Ranged (X m) You may make a ranged weapon attack up to X m.
Set If you did not move this round: gain +1d8 weapon damage.
Thrown (X m) You may make a ranged attack by throwing the weapon up to X m (you must retrieve it afterward unless a rule says otherwise).
Load After you fire, the weapon is Unloaded. To fire again, spend 1 Attack Action to reload it. You need one free hand to do so. Quick Load may instead use Movement as described in the Movement rules.
Defensive While wielding this weapon two-handed, add your Mastery (max +6) to your Evade.
Spell Focus (+Xd8) When you deal damage with a Power that has the Spell tag, add +Xd8 bonus damage dice. This does not add damage to non-damaging Spells.

Magic is not a separate family of Powers. It is a delivery method.

A Spell uses an existing eligible Power template and changes how that Power is delivered and resisted. The underlying Power remains the same mechanical Power.

A Spell keeps the Power's:

  • Power Level
  • printed Range
  • Damage
  • AoE
  • Duration
  • Specials
  • action type
  • base Technical Reference

Only the delivery changes.

A Martial delivery uses a weapon, body, tool, physical technique, or another non-Spell method and normally resolves through an Attack Roll where applicable.

A Spell delivery gains the Spell tag, uses a fixed Casting Attribute, and resolves through the Casting Roll and Spell TN rules below.

Changing delivery does not create a second Power for duplicate selection or the once-per-Round Power Use Limit. A Martial and Spell version with the same base Technical Reference are still the same Power for those rules.

Spell Design Rule

Only a Ranged Active may use Spell delivery unless a specific rule explicitly allows another Power structure to become a Spell.

Melee-only, Self-only, melee-reach, and close-combat Powers do not become ranged merely because they gain the Spell tag.

A Ranged Active with one or more Specials may use Spell delivery normally.

A character may also possess a limited number of Special-less Spell Powers. The number of character-owned Spell Powers that contain no Special cannot exceed the character's Mastery Rank.

This means a character may use Spell delivery for ordinary structures such as a damage-only Single Target Attack, Split Attack, Restoration Power, or another legal Ranged Active without a Special, but only up to that Mastery Rank limit.

Spell Powers that already contain at least one Special do not count against the Special-less Spell limit.

A source may explicitly grant a Spell without counting against this limit.

Catalogue Delivery Conversion

Ranged Active catalogue entries may be written using a Martial baseline even when the same Technical Reference can use Spell delivery. When a legal Ranged Active changes from Martial to Spell delivery:

  • a printed Ranged Weapon or Thrown Weapon requirement applies only to the Martial version and is replaced by the normal Spell delivery requirements,
  • Attack Pool / Attack Roll becomes Casting Pool / Casting Roll,
  • Evade becomes the affected creature's Final Spell TN,
  • weapon damage is omitted because it is delivery-specific,
  • printed Power damage, Specials, Range, AoE, Duration, target count, split structure, control, and other non-delivery effects remain unchanged,
  • and Spell Focus applies normally when the resulting Spell is damaging.

These substitutions do not create a second Power. They are the Spell delivery of the same base Technical Reference.

Shared Power Effects and Delivery-Specific Effects

Unless a rule explicitly names a delivery-specific property, a legal effect may interact with Martial and Spell delivery alike.

Examples:

  • Critical may apply to a Martial Attack or damaging Spell.
  • Special Boost may increase Specials applied through Martial or Spell delivery.
  • Raises (Intellect Stone Ability) grants one shared allowance of 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 at Ranks 1–4 for the current Round. Choose how many to use before each eligible roll and choose their effects after a successful roll. They neither increase TN nor require Raise Cost; on success they apply, on failure they are consumed without effect.
  • Extra Attack grants additional Attack Actions that may be used with any otherwise legal unused Active, including Spells.

Delivery-specific rules remain delivery-specific:

  • Weapon Damage, Damage (Might Stone Ability), and effects that explicitly require a weapon or Martial Attack do not become Spell effects.
  • Spell Focus and Spell Resistance apply only to Spells.
  • A rule that explicitly refers to an Attack Roll does not automatically modify a Casting Roll, and vice versa, unless that rule says it works with both.

Casting Attribute

When a Power gains Spell delivery, choose whether it uses:

  • Intellect
  • Resolve
  • Influence

This choice is part of the Spell's design and is fixed for that Spell.

Casting Roll

Casting while threatened: If the caster is within any enemy's Melee Reach at declaration, every legal Spell Casting Roll is made with Disadvantage, whether the Spell damages, restores Scarred Health Bars, cleanses, supports, controls, creates a zone, or otherwise resolves through Casting. This includes any otherwise legal melee-/touch-range Spell and any self-targeted legal Spell. It does not reduce Healing Dice, change the Spell Base TN, or make prohibited deliveries legal. Multiple enemies do not stack this Disadvantage. See Threatened Ranged Attacks for the common timing and Reaction rules.

When casting a Spell, roll:

Casting Attribute k Mastery

The Casting Attribute is the Attribute chosen when the Spell was designed: Intellect, Resolve, or Influence.

Spells do not roll against the target's Evade.

Every Spell uses a Spell Base TN determined by the caster's Mastery Rank.

Mastery Rank Spell Base TN
I 6
II 14
III 22
IV 30
V 38
VI 46
VII 54
VIII 62

For a Spell that affects a creature, determine that creature's Final Spell TN:

Final Spell TN = Spell Base TN + Target Spell Resistance

Apply eligible reductions first, including Passive: Spell Resistance Piercing (ceil(PL / 2)) for that caster's own Spells. Count no less than 0 remaining Spell Resistance; the target's actual resistance and Spell Base TN remain unchanged.

For a direct Spell, compare the Casting Roll against the target's Final Spell TN.

For a Spell with the AoE tag, make one Casting Roll for the entire area. Compare that same result separately against the Final Spell TN of each valid creature in the area.

Each creature is checked independently using its own Spell Resistance.

Spell AoEs do not use Evade, but they do use Spell Resistance. Legal defenses that explicitly work against a Spell AoE, such as Dive for Cover, still function normally.

Casting Success and Resistance

The Spell Base TN determines whether the caster successfully produces the Spell. Spell Resistance determines whether a successfully produced Spell affects a specific creature.

  • If the Casting Roll is below Spell Base TN, the Spell fizzles. There is no additional penalty.
  • If the Casting Roll reaches Spell Base TN, the Spell is successfully cast.
  • A creature is affected only if that same result also reaches its Final Spell TN.
  • If the roll reaches Spell Base TN but not a creature's Final Spell TN, that creature resists the Spell. The Spell does not fizzle.
  • For an AoE Spell, resistance by one creature does not affect any other creature.

A Spell that creates or places an effect without directly affecting a creature must reach Spell Base TN to be created.

Willing Spell Targets

A creature that is aware of a Spell and willingly accepts it may choose to treat its Spell Resistance as 0 against that Spell. The choice is made before the Casting Roll. Spell Base TN is never reduced this way.

This allows willing healing, support, and beneficial Spells to function without making Spell Resistance a penalty to their intended recipient.

Persistent Spell Zones

When Spell delivery creates a Persistent Diminishing Zone, make one Casting Roll when the zone is created (including threatened Disadvantage if applicable at that declaration) and record the final result. Later zone applications use the stored result and do not cause new Casting Rolls or new threatened Disadvantage.

  • If the result is below Spell Base TN, the zone is not created. There is no additional penalty.
  • If the result reaches Spell Base TN, the zone is created for its normal Duration.
  • Whenever a creature would be affected by that zone, compare the stored Casting result against that creature's current Final Spell TN.
  • A creature whose Final Spell TN is not reached resists that application; the zone remains.
  • The zone's normal once-per-Round application limit still applies.

Spell Conversion Summary

A Spell is an eligible Power using magical delivery.

The Spell tag changes how the Power is delivered and resisted. It does not replace the Power's underlying effect structure or create a second copy of the Power.

A Spell may therefore be damage-only, healing-only, utility-oriented, or Special-based if the underlying Ranged Active is legal. Special-less Spells are limited to a number equal to the character's Mastery Rank; Spells that already contain Specials do not count against that limit.

Powers are the mechanical building blocks of character abilities. This chapter does not explain every Special again. Specials are defined in their own rules chapter. Instead, this chapter explains the main Power types and points to the dedicated Power catalogues.

A Power belongs to one of the following categories:

  • Actives
  • Passives
  • Active Buffs
  • Reactions
  • Movement Powers

Each category has its own design rules, limits, timing, and pricing logic.

Power Use Limit

A specific Power can be used only once per round. After you use a Power, that Power is considered spent until the start of the next round. The Power's identity is its base Technical Reference, not its character-facing name, source, or current PL. Changing between Martial and Spell delivery does not create a second Power identity; delivery method is not a way to bypass duplicate rules or the once-per-Round Power Use Limit.

This applies to all Power Types:

  • Actives
  • Active Buffs
  • Reactions
  • Movement Powers
  • other named Power effects

Passive Powers are not “used” each round unless they contain a specific activated or triggered effect. If you gain extra Attack Actions, extra Reactions, or extra Movement, you may use them only with Powers that have not already been used this round. Additional Attack Actions from multiple sources do not stack unless a rule explicitly says otherwise; use the highest single grant of additional Attack Actions. You cannot use the same Active Power multiple times in the same round. You cannot use the same Reaction multiple times in the same round unless that Reaction explicitly allows repeated uses. Each repeated use still costs 1 Reaction and does not grant additional Reactions. You cannot use the same Active Buff multiple times in the same round. To attack multiple times with Powers in the same round, you need multiple different Active Powers. To react multiple times in the same round, you need multiple different valid Reactions and enough Reaction uses. To move with multiple Movement Powers in the same round, you need multiple different Movement Powers and enough Movement uses. Basic Attacks are not Powers and may be repeated if you have enough Attack Actions.

Power Categories

Power Type Purpose Primary Use Catalogue
Actives Direct actions, attacks, effects, zones, barriers, and Special delivery. Your main action-based tools. Actives
Passives Always-on character identity and reliable baseline benefits. Permanent or pre-selected character traits. Passives
Active Buffs Temporary combat states that enhance the user or allies for a limited time. Stances, short-term boosts, protection, escalation. Active Buffs
Reactions Immediate answers to a specific trigger. One-hit defense, interception, emergency protection, counters. Reactions
Movement Powers Alternative movement modes. Dash, leap, teleport, flight, safe movement, burrow, phase passage. Movement

Mechanical Powers and Character Expression

You pay for what your character can do, not for what your character looks like.

Powers in this system are written as mechanical templates. A Power's listed name describes what the Power does mechanically. It does not define what the Power looks like, sounds like, feels like, or means for the character. Players are encouraged to rename, describe, and flavor their Powers to match their character. The same mechanical Power may look completely different for different characters.

Examples:

  • A Ranged Single Target Attack may be an arrow, a thrown knife, a lightning bolt, a shard of glass, a beam of moonlight, a dragon spark, or a poisonous thorn.
  • A Melee Push / Pull may be a shield bash, a hammer blow, a gravity pulse, a burst of wind, or a spectral beast strike.
  • A Mental Attack may be a psychic lance, a whispered curse, a memory spike, a pressure wave of fear, or a silent scream.
  • A Mind Illusion may be a nightmare image, a false wall, a phantom voice, a distorted reflection, a veil of insects, or a hallucinated enemy.
  • A Heal may be divine light, blood magic, herbal restoration, ancestral warmth, repairing nanogrowth, or stolen life returned.

The mechanics stay the same.

The fiction belongs to the player.

Player-Named Powers

When a player chooses a Power, they may give it a character-facing name.

The technical name remains the rules reference.

The character-facing name is used in play, on the character sheet, and in narration.

Example:

Technical Power: Mental Attack
Character Power Name: Psychic Lance

Technical Power: Ranged Single Target Special: Ruin
Character Power Name: Blackfire Arrow

Technical Power: Mind Illusion
Character Power Name: The Wall That Was Never There

Technical Power: Melee Push / Pull
Character Power Name: Titanbreaker Blow

A character-facing Power name does not change the Power's mechanics.

Power identity follows the technical name across every source, including purchases, Echo Artifacts, other Artifacts, Trees, and granted abilities. Two character-facing names with the same Technical Reference are the same Power for duplicate selection and the once-per-round Power Use Limit. Changing between Martial and Spell delivery does not create a new Power identity.

If a player describes a Power in a way that sounds stronger than its rules text, use the rules text.

If a player describes a Power in a way that sounds weaker, stranger, or more personal, the description is allowed as long as the mechanics remain clear.

Actives

Actives are action-based Powers.

They are used to attack, apply Specials, create areas, shape the battlefield, create barriers, or produce another immediate effect. Actives are the main place where Special delivery happens. Most combat Powers that directly affect enemies, spaces, or battlefield objects are Actives.

Actives may include:

  • damage,
  • healing,
  • Specials,
  • AoE,
  • persistent zones,
  • barriers,
  • control effects,
  • forced movement,
  • utility effects,
  • or other paid mechanical effects.

Actives use their own Power templates and PP structure.

See: Actives

Passives

Passives are reliable, always-on character identity. They do not require an action to activate. Every current Passive belongs to exactly one Passive Category. Combined Passives are not available in this release.
A Passive Category is a mechanical classification, not flavour text.

The authoritative 28-Passive catalogue includes defenses such as Armor, Evade, Health/Fortitude, Temporary HP, Parry and Damage Negation; offensive choices such as Damage, Armor Reduction, Critical, Maximization, Enemy Evade Reduction, Spell Resistance Piercing and Special Amplification; plus Self Cleanse, Regeneration, Speed and other support Powers. Passive: Regeneration, not a generic "Healing" Passive, handles its printed Scarred-Bar recovery.

Offensive / Defensive / Utility & Mobility selection groups are for display only; mechanical Passive Categories still determine slot compatibility.

Passives may not hide Active effects inside always-on features. They may not grant free attacks, extra actions, Movement Powers, Reactions, Spell effects, full Persistent Zones, or casual hard control. See: Passives

Active Buffs

Active Buffs are temporary combat enhancements that are activated during the Preparation Phase, before the Combat Round begins.

Activation Cost: Activating an Active Buff consumes the character's base Attack Action for the upcoming Round. This Action is committed during Preparation and cannot be used during that character's Turn, whether for a Basic Attack, an Active Power, or another action requiring it.

Additional Attack Actions granted by Stones or other legal sources remain available. The same base Attack Action cannot be spent or forfeited a second time to pay for another effect.

Activation and Duration: The Active Buff becomes effective at the beginning of the upcoming Round, before any creature takes its Turn. It normally lasts Mastery Rank complete Rounds.

The activation Round counts as the first Round. At Round End of the final Round, the Buff expires. Its duration is independent of the activating character's Initiative or Turn.

Maintenance and Replacement: A character may normally maintain only one Active Buff and may activate or replace an Active Buff only during a Preparation Phase. Replacing an existing Buff ends the previous Buff. Active Buffs cannot stack with themselves.

Round-Based Resources: Resources granted by an Active Buff for each Round become available during the activation Preparation Phase and refresh once during each subsequent Preparation Phase while the Buff remains active. Unused Round-based resources expire at Round End.

Other effects with explicitly defined triggers, such as Start of Turn or End of Turn, retain those triggers unless the specific Buff states otherwise.

Active Buffs cannot be activated or replaced during a creature's Turn or through an ordinary Attack Action. Explicit exceptions must be stated in their own rules.

Active Buff Limits

Apply the Preparation Phase activation and replacement rules above: at most one activation or replacement each Round, one maintained Buff, and no self-stacking. Only an explicit written exception may override a limit.

Active Buffs may be:

  • single-focus defensive buffs,
  • single-focus offensive buffs,
  • single-effect aura buffs,
  • or dedicated premium subsystem buffs.

Combined Active Buffs are not selectable in this beta release.

Active Buffs do not apply Specials by default.

Active Buffs in this catalogue do not apply or increase numeric Specials. Passive: Special Amplification, Intellect Stone Ability: Special Boost, and the Special Increase Raise Effect are separate legal sources; none is a Combined Active Buff.

See: Active Buffs

Reactions

Reactions are immediate answers to a specific trigger.

A Reaction is not a second turn.
A Reaction is not a hidden Attack Action.
A Reaction is not a way to add free offensive pressure outside your turn.

A Reaction costs your Reaction for the round.

You may normally use only one Reaction per round.

Reactions answer narrow moments such as:

  • you are attacked,
  • you are hit,
  • you would take damage,
  • an ally nearby is attacked,
  • you fail a defensive moment,
  • or a premium defensive subsystem is triggered.

If a Reaction grants Armor, Evade, Temporary HP, Damage Reduction, or Phasing, that benefit applies only to the triggering event unless the entry explicitly says otherwise.

Reactions do not apply or increase Specials by default.

See: Reactions

Movement Powers

Movement Powers replace your normal Movement for the round.

They are used to change:

  • how you move,
  • where you can move,
  • or what kind of path you may take.

A Movement Power is not an Attack Action.
A Movement Power is not an Active Buff.
A Movement Power is not a Reaction.
A Movement Power is not a Special-delivery system.

When you use a Movement Power, the listed distance is your total Movement for that Movement Power.

It is not added on top of your normal Movement unless the entry explicitly says otherwise.

Movement Powers may include movement types such as:

  • Ground Dash,
  • Safe Movement,
  • Teleport,
  • Teleport with Ally,
  • Flight,
  • Leap,
  • Wall Walk,
  • Burrow,
  • Phase Passage,
  • or Trample.

See: Movement

Form and Transformation

Form describes how a character looks: human, wolf, bear, a clawed monster, or another suitable appearance. Every Form uses one character sheet with the same purchased Attributes, Skills, Powers, Stone Abilities, attacks, Damage, Armor, Health, senses, Movement, Reach, Range, and occupied Hexes.

A character may describe or change their Form freely, including during combat, without an Action, Stone cost, use limit, or activation time. Features such as keen scent, special vision, claws, flight, or a powerful bite use the corresponding abilities already purchased on the character sheet.

Transformation changes a creature's actual size and occupied Hex footprint. Its mechanical consequences are specified by the applicable Growth rule. Polymorph and True Polymorph are not separate Powers: appearance changes use Form, and changes to occupied Hexes use Transformation.

  • Uses: A character may activate a size-changing Transformation Mastery Rank times per Safe Haven Rest. Each transformation into a larger footprint uses one use; selecting a different visual Form does not.
  • Activation: A Transformation takes only a few moments and costs no Stones by itself. It has no fixed duration.
  • In combat: Choose the Transformation before combat. The occupied footprint stays fixed until combat ends. Visual Form may still change freely.
  • Return: Outside combat, returning to original size is free. Becoming Incapacitated immediately returns the character to original size while all injuries and Incapacitated remain in effect.
  • Size direction: Transformation expands the original footprint; the character may return to their original footprint outside combat. The original footprint is the minimum size.
  • Space: The entire larger footprint must fit in free, traversable Hexes. Occupied or blocked Hexes prevent Growth; creatures and obstacles keep their positions.

Growth grants its explicitly defined, purchased mechanical benefits. The character retains all other purchased abilities; its appearance determines none of their values.

Growth Geometry and Combat Effects

Growth G adds G complete Hex rings around the character's original single-Hex space. A creature at Growth G occupies 1 + 3 × G × (G + 1) Hexes. Each ring adds accessible surrounding space and increases how many adjacent creatures may engage the transformed character.

Growth Occupied Hexes Adjacent Hexes Total Base Melee Reach Additional 0-Penalty Health Bars Push/Pull Reduction Physical Ranged and Spell Range
0 1 6 2 m 0 0 Normal
1 7 12 4 m 1 MR × 1 m Normal
2 19 18 6 m 2 MR × 2 m ×2
3 37 24 8 m 3 MR × 3 m ×2

Melee Reach: Add 2 m per Growth to the normal 2 m base. Measure reach and ranged distances for a multi-Hex creature from the nearest edge of its occupied Hex footprint to the target, using the normal distance rules; weapon Reach and eligible bonuses add normally. Physical Ranged means bow, crossbow, thrown weapon and comparable physical ranged attacks. At Growth 2 or higher, their Range and Spell Range are each doubled once, never again at later Growth steps. Apply any additional flat range bonuses under their normal rules.

Push/Pull: Subtract Growth × the transformed character's Mastery Rank in meters from each incoming Push or Pull distance, to a minimum of 0 m. Other effects of the hit resolve normally.

Space and targeting: Every occupied Hex must remain traversable through movement and fit when transforming. Growth leaves nearby creatures and obstacles in place. An AoE affecting several of a creature's occupied Hexes still resolves once against that creature. Growth changes the footprint, Reach, Range and Health Bars specified here; other combat values are those purchased on the character sheet.

Growth Health Bars

A size-changing Transformation with Growth G provides G additional 0-penalty Health Bars before the character's regular Healthy Bar. Each Growth Bar has Vitality × 4 HP and is damaged before normal Health Bars. All Growth Bars must become Scarred before damage progresses into the normal bars. Growth Bars do not increase the size of normal bars and grant no inherent Armor or Temporary HP.

Each Growth Bar keeps its own damage and Scarred state across transformations. Returning to original size merely hides the Growth Bars; it does not heal, restore, or reset them. Transforming to Growth again makes the corresponding bars available in precisely their previous state. A Scarred Growth Bar remains Scarred and is skipped as usual until restored by the existing recovery rules. A hidden Scarred Growth Bar remains eligible for Safe Haven Rest, Natural Recovery, Remove Scar or Restoration; the player may choose it whenever that recovery permits choosing an eligible Scarred Health Bar. Reopening a hidden Growth Bar does not change the character's current size. Partially damaged Growth Bars likewise retain that damage. Changing size leaves normal Health Bars unchanged.

Defensive Effects

Armor, Evade, Health Bars, Temporary HP, Damage Reduction, Phasing, Anti-Displacement and the different forms of recovery belong to distinct defensive or restorative mechanics.

Use the relevant Power or Stone Ability for the listed effect:

Effect Usually Found In
Armor Passives, Active Buffs, Reactions
Evade Passives, Active Buffs, Reactions
Health Bars Passives
Temporary HP Passives, Active Buffs, Reactions
Ordinary HP Healing Resolve: Healing (Stone Ability); Damage Transfer
Scarred-Bar Restoration Restoration Actives and Artifact-granted Restoration
Self Regeneration Passive: Regeneration
Damage Reduction Dedicated Passive, Active Buff, and Reaction entries
Phasing Dedicated Passive, Active Buff, and Reaction entries
Anti-Displacement Passives, Active Buffs, Reactions, or specific Tree exceptions

These effects are explained in the relevant catalogue entries, not in this chapter.

Movement Powers provoke movement-triggered Reactions normally unless the entry explicitly says otherwise.

Only Movement Powers that say they prevent such Reactions do so.

See: Movement

Closed Premium Subsystems

Some mechanics are closed premium subsystems.

They may only appear in their dedicated Power entries.

The most important closed premium subsystems are:

  • Damage Reduction
  • Phasing

Damage Reduction and Phasing may not be casually added as secondary riders.

They may not be bundled into unrelated Powers under a different name.

They may only appear where the dedicated catalogue entry explicitly allows them.

Minor Expressions are small supernatural expressions of awakened Attributes.

They are not Powers.
They are not Spells.
They are not combat techniques.

They are minor manifestations of what a high Attribute means in the fiction. Minor Expressions support, color, and enable scenes. They do not replace Powers.

Unlocking Minor Expressions

Minor Expressions are tied to Attributes.

The following Attributes have Minor Expressions:

  • Might
  • Agility
  • Intellect
  • Resolve
  • Influence
  • Wits

Vitality does not have Minor Expressions. To choose a Minor Expression from an Attribute, that Attribute must be at least 4. If an Attribute is lower than 4, its Minor Expressions are not available.

Minor Expression Limit

A character may choose a total number of Minor Expressions equal to their Mastery Rank.

This is a global limit across all Attributes.

Example:

A Mastery Rank 2 character may choose 2 Minor Expressions total. These may both come from the same eligible Attribute, or from different eligible Attributes, as long as each chosen Expression belongs to an Attribute with a value of at least 4.

Attribute Tiers

Minor Expressions grow automatically with the Attribute that unlocks them. Each Minor Expression has five possible tiers:

Current Attribute Value Expression Tier
1-3 Unavailable
4-7 Tier 4
8-11 Tier 8
12-15 Tier 12
16-19 Tier 16
20-40 Tier 20

Use the highest tier whose threshold the Attribute has reached. These are the compressed 1-40 Attribute scale thresholds, converted from the previous wider Attribute scale; do not use obsolete thresholds such as 8/16/24/32 for this progression. Values 21-40 continue to use Tier 20; no sixth Minor Expression tier exists.

Example:

A character with Intellect 11 uses the Tier 8 version of their Intellect Minor Expressions.

A character with Might 4 uses the Tier 4 version of their Might Minor Expressions.

If the Attribute later increases, the Minor Expression improves automatically.

Reroll Point Cost

If the character has a Reroll Point pool, choosing a new Minor Expression costs 1 current Reroll Point.

Removing a Minor Expression refunds 1 Reroll Point, up to the character’s maximum Reroll Points.

If the character does not have enough current Reroll Points to choose a new Minor Expression, they cannot choose it.

If the character has no Reroll Point pool, choosing Minor Expressions has no Reroll Point cost.

Using Minor Expressions

Minor Expressions are used outside direct combat resolution.

They may help a character:

  • create a small opening,
  • color a scene,
  • justify a Skill Check,
  • notice something subtle,
  • influence the tone of a moment,
  • overcome a minor obstacle,
  • or express their awakened nature in the fiction.

Minor Expressions do not automatically replace Skill Checks.

If the outcome is uncertain, opposed, dangerous, or dramatically important, the GM may still call for a normal Skill Check.

A Minor Expression may support the method of a Skill Check, but it does not replace the Skill, the roll, or the normal consequences of failure.

Combat Limitation

Minor Expressions are not combat Powers.

They do not grant attacks, damage, Evade, Armor, healing, movement replacement, Reactions, or Action economy unless a specific rule explicitly says so.

The GM may allow a Minor Expression during a combat scene if it is used for description, positioning, interaction, intimidation, escape setup, or environmental interaction.

However, it should never replace an Active Power, Passive, Active Buff, Reaction, Movement Power, or combat maneuver.
